standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of the set of associated primes of a finite module
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-lemma-finite-ass, invoked at proof line 3722
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that the set of associated primes of the fibre module is finite, so that they can be listed and split according to whether they are contained in the given prime.

core_obligations: List and split the associated primes: by finiteness write them as a finite set and, after renumbering, separate those contained in the given prime from those which are not (proof lines 3719-3731).

Produce an element of the fibre separating them: the product of the associated primes not contained in the given prime is not contained in that prime because the latter is prime, so one may pick an element of the fibre lying in those primes but not in the given prime (proof lines 3732-3737).

Lift the element: an element of the fibre may always be scaled by a nonzero element of the residue field of the base point so that it becomes the image of an element of the algebra, and that lift satisfies the required conditions (proof lines 3738-3741).
proof_roadmap: List the finite set of associated primes and split it (proof lines 3719-3731).
Pick an element of the product not in the given prime (proof lines 3732-3737).
Scale and lift to the algebra (proof lines 3738-3741).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a finitely presented module over a finitely presented algebra, an element of the algebra not in a given prime whose image in the fibre lies in every associated prime of the fibre module that does not contain the given prime (statement lines 3704-3717, tag 05IF-adjacent). The proof lists the finitely many associated primes, splits them relative to the given prime, picks an element of the product of those not contained in it (possible because the given prime is prime), and then scales that element by a nonzero element of the residue field so that it lifts to the algebra. The lifting step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
